obligations.subject: fresh allocation and become
obligations.question: Verify primary-source distinctions between creation, fresh address allocation, and behavior replacement.
obligations.decision: Verified. LAW (Agha 1986 ch. 3-5; AMST 1997 sec. 2-4): creation allocates a mail address fresh with respect to the configuration and installs an initial behavior; become replaces the current actor's behavior only and never allocates. The two operations are orthogonal in the operational semantics. DERIVED (Bombay): Create carries a creator-local nonce so the creating transition can refer to its staged child without performing allocation in the pure fold; CreationKind records lifecycle provenance as data. POLICY (Bombay): interpreters install a transition's creates before interpreting that transition's sends and local observation requests; replacement at an existing address is deliberately absent and stable identity is derived via a proxy actor.

obligations.question: Assess independence, boundaries, and applicable state-space coverage.
obligations.decision: Retain the test architecture as-is; the reference models are genuinely independent and the state-space coverage is layered (exhaustive + property + fuzz). Independence: crates/behavior-testkit/src/model.rs states in its module doc that the supervision Model 'encodes the DOCUMENTED contract ... written from the spec, never from implementation branches'; it uses deliberately different state and vocabulary from the implementation — IncarnationModel has occupied/vacant/queued_successor versus Proxy's worker/worker_alive/pending (model.rs:86-155 vs supervising.rs:208-214), ExpectedCreation Initial/Ordinary/Successor versus CreationKind Birth/ReplacementIncarnation (model.rs:68-83), InactivityModel token pairs versus ReceiveTimeout's generation state (model.rs:16-58), and Model::apply re-derives eligibility/window/candidate/budget logic from the contract (model.rs:280-351) rather than calling Supervising. Boundary coverage: exhaustive.rs enumerates every sequence of up to three child-stopped events over a two-slot fleet across all 3 strategies x 3 policies x 7 outcomes x budgets x window edges (AT_VALUES [0,2] straddle the window) against Model; supervision_model.rs runs 512-case proptests against the same Model plus budget-window aging edges; stash_properties.rs pairs a random filter model with an exhaustive sequence check; fsm_properties.rs and two_buffer.rs assert the black-box no-drop/no-duplication reconciliation recorded+held==stepped without any reference model (implementation-vocabulary-free); cross_lane.rs proves lane isolation in a supervised stash stack; shutdown_model.rs checks a first-request prefix model. Classification: the models are Bombay-derived test constructions whose laws are the documented contracts; no test reimplements production logic as its own oracle.

obligations.decision: Retain current compile-fail coverage as-is: one compile_fail doctest plus structurally unrepresentable negative space. The doctest at behavior.rs:412-418 (on the Behavior trait) proves effect and termination escape seats are intentionally absent — erased_effect<B: Behavior>() -> PhantomData<B::Effect> fails to compile, guarding the closed effect algebra against any future associated-type addition; `cargo test --doc -p bombay-behavior` runs it green. No trybuild/ui harness exists (no trybuild in any Cargo.toml; grep across manifests is empty) and none is required for the remaining invariant classes, because the other capability/phase/birth/composition invariants are inhabited-type impossibilities rather than compiler lints: a phase transition outside the menu is unconstructible when Ph = Never (Step::Goto(Never) has no value, verdict.rs:6-10 doc, enum at :11 — 'The law is the type, not a convention'); a birth from a NoBirths behavior needs Create<A, Never>, whose child field is uninhabited (NoBirths at behavior.rs:291, Births<C> at :299); a composition missing a lane bound (e.g. B::Event: ChildEvent on Supervising, supervising.rs:628) fails at the composition site with a trait-bound error naming the missing capability. Positive static probes lock the forwarding side: algebra.rs:19 requires_no_births, :34 requires_births, :40 requires_worker_events and the test birth_modes_are_disjoint_and_wrappers_forward_them (:331) compile only while wrappers forward capability seats truthfully — these are compile-time assertions whose failure mode is a broken build. Honest gap assessment: negative compile-fail coverage exists only for the effect-seat invariant; adding a trybuild suite for the uninhabited-type invariants would test the type system itself rather than Behavior code, so the deliberate single-doctest policy is retained.
